requested_operation: implement separately importable optional NumPy and PyTorch adapters with explicit dtype, device, copy, and optional-dependency behavior

inputs.root_cause: The NumPy adapter's copy policy was implicit, while the PyTorch adapter routed a read-only NumPy view into a mutable tensor, accepted copy=False without a safety contract, had no device parameter, inherited NumPy's narrower dtype behavior, and did not handle empty tensors explicitly.
inputs.affected_layer: SafeTensors optional framework adapters, installed-wheel behavior, and adapter documentation

observations: to_torch(copy=False) did not reject an unsafe mutable alias over a read-only payload
to_torch(..., device='cuda:1') raised TypeError because device was not part of the API
an empty tensor was routed through the NumPy bridge without an explicit shaped empty-tensor path
an unavailable PyTorch dtype leaked the NumPy adapter's error instead of reporting the PyTorch capability boundary

implementation.optional_import_isolation: base and adapter-module imports load neither NumPy nor PyTorch; frameworks are imported only when the conversion function is called
implementation.numpy_copy_false: returns a read-only C-order view borrowed from the document payload; the document lifetime remains binding
implementation.numpy_copy_true: returns an independent writable C-order copy
implementation.numpy_dtype_policy: requires an exact NumPy storage dtype and rejects unsupported BF16, float8, and sub-byte types rather than reinterpreting bytes
implementation.torch_copy_policy: copy=True is the safe default and copy=False is rejected because PyTorch exposes mutable tensors but SafeTensors path payloads are read-only memory maps
implementation.torch_storage: copies tensor bytes into an independent writable bytearray and constructs the CPU tensor with torch.frombuffer
implementation.torch_device_policy: optional device is passed to tensor.to after safe CPU construction; framework device parsing and transfer errors remain PyTorch's responsibility
implementation.torch_dtype_policy: maps exact framework dtype attributes dynamically and rejects dtypes unavailable in the installed PyTorch version
implementation.empty_tensor_policy: uses torch.empty with the exact descriptor shape and dtype because frombuffer cannot construct a tensor from an empty buffer
implementation.endianness_policy: fails explicitly on non-little-endian hosts rather than silently interpreting SafeTensors little-endian bytes in native order
implementation.tradeoff: PyTorch zero-copy is deliberately unavailable; this sacrifices a potential CPU performance optimization to avoid writable aliases over immutable bytes and read-only memory maps
